zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Najm
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والنَّجْمِ إذا هَوى﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, swore by the star (al-najm).
And His saying: ﴿ما ضَلَّ صاحِبُكُمْ﴾ [al-Najm: 2] is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). It has come in the exegesis that al-najm is the Pleiades (al-thurayyā), and that is what the Arabs call it. It has also come in the exegesis that al-najm is the descent of the Qurʾān in instalments (najm after najm): a verse or two of it would come down at a time, and between the beginning of its revelation and its completion were twenty years. And one of the philologists said: "اَلنَّجْمُ" is in the sense of "اَلنُّجُومُ" (the stars), and they recited:
؎فَباتَتْ تَعُدُّ النَّجْمَ في مُسْتَحِيرَةٍ ∗∗∗ سَرِيعٍ بِأيْدِي الآكِلِينَ جُمُودُها
(She spent the night counting the stars in a brimming pot, whose fat quickly congeals on the hands of those who eat.)
He is describing a cooking pot rich in fat. The meaning of "تَعُدُّ النَّجْمَ" is: because of the clearness of its fat she sees the stars in it; al-mustaḥīra is the cooking pot. And he said: "The fat congeals on the hands because of its abundance." And they said: similar to it is ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 75]. The meaning of ﴿إذا هَوى﴾ is: when it falls; and if its meaning is the descent of the Qurʾān, then the meaning of "إذا هَوى" is: when it descends.
﴿ما ضَلَّ صاحِبُكم وما غَوى﴾ [al-Najm: 2]: meaning the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿فَأوْحى إلى عَبْدِهِ ما أوْحى﴾, that is: Jibrīl revealed to the Prophet, peace be upon him, what he revealed.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿ما كَذَبَ الفُؤادُ ما رَأى﴾, and it has also been read "ما كَذَّبَ الفُؤادُ ما رَأى", with a doubled (mushaddad) dhāl.

zajjaj:12-12.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَتُمارُونَهُ عَلى ما يَرى﴾, and "أفَتَمْرُونَهُ" and ﴿أفَتُمارُونَهُ﴾ — it has been read both ways. Whoever reads "أفَتَمْرُونَهُ", the meaning is: "Do you then deny him?"; and whoever reads ﴿أفَتُمارُونَهُ﴾, its meaning is: do you dispute with him over his having seen Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, with his heart, and over his having seen the greatest of His signs?!

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَـزْلَةً أُخْرى﴾ ﴿عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ المُنْتَهى﴾ [al-Najm: 14], that is: he saw him another time at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
﴿عِنْدَها جَنَّةُ المَأْوى﴾: it has come in the exegesis that it is a garden to which the souls of the martyrs go. When He had narrated these accounts, and made known, Mighty and Majestic is He, how Jibrīl narrated it, and that this comes to the Prophet ﷺ from Allah, like unto Whom there is nothing, it was said to them: ﴿أفَرَأيْتُمُ اللاتَ والعُزّى﴾ [al-Najm: 19] ﴿وَمَناةَ الثّالِثَةَ الأُخْرى﴾ [al-Najm: 20]. It is as if the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Tell us about these gods of yours which you worship besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: do they have any of this power and grandeur with which the Lord of Might, Majestic and Mighty is He, has been described?" It has come in the exegesis that al-Lāt was an idol belonging to Thaqīf which they worshipped; that al-ʿUzzā was a samura, which is a tree belonging to Ghaṭafān which they worshipped; and that Manāt was a rock belonging to Hudhayl and Khuzāʿa which they worshipped besides Allah. So it was said to them: Tell us about these gods which you worship, and alongside which you worship the angels, claiming that the angels and these are the daughters of Allah. So Allah rebuked them, saying: Have you considered these females — do they belong to Allah while you choose males? And that is His saying: ﴿ألَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ ولَهُ الأُنْثى﴾ [al-Najm: 21].
Whoever reads "أفَرَأيْتُمُ اللّاتَّ والعُزّى", with a doubled tāʾ — they claimed that a man used to mix (yalittu) sawīq (barley meal) and sell it beside that idol, so the idol was called "اَللّاتُّ", with a doubled tāʾ. The majority reading is "اَللّاتُ", with a single (unstressed) tāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī used to pause on it with hāʾ, saying "اَللّاهْ", and this is according to analogy (qiyās), but the better course here is to follow the muṣḥaf and pause on it with tāʾ.
And it has also been read "عِنْدَها جَنَّهُ المَهْوى", with hāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the variant usually reported is جَنَّهُ المَأْوى, with the pronoun hāʾ ("covered him").]», but the better reading is ﴿جَنَّةُ المَأْوى﴾, because it has come in the exegesis — as we mentioned — that the souls of the martyrs dwell in it.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ما زاغَ البَصَرُ وما طَغى﴾, that is: "The sight of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not swerve, nor did it transgress", i.e. it did not deviate nor go beyond the mark in his seeing Jibrīl, who had filled the horizon.

zajjaj:18-18.t: And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ رَأى مِن آياتِ رَبِّهِ الكُبْرى﴾: it has come in the exegesis that the Prophet ﷺ saw his Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He, with his heart, and that this is a favour with which he was singled out, just as Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, was singled out with intimate friendship (al-khulla). And it has been said: he saw a mighty matter; and its explanation is: "He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord."

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تِلْكَ إذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزى﴾, that is: your assigning daughters to Allah and sons to yourselves. "اَلضِّيزى" in the speech of the Arabs means deficient, unjust. One says "ḍāzahu, yaḍīzuhu" when he cuts short his right, and one also says "ḍaʾazahu, yaḍʾazuhu", with hamza. The grammarians are agreed that the origin of "ضِيزى" is "ضُوزى", and their argument is that it was shifted from the pattern "فُعْلى" to "فِعْلى", from "ضُوزى" to "ضِيزى", so that the yāʾ might be preserved, just as they said "أبْيَضُ" (white) and "بِيضٌ" (plural), whose origin is "بُوضٌ", and the ḍamma was changed into a kasra.
And I read with one of the scholars of the language several dialectal forms of "ضِيزى": one says "ضِيزى", "ضُوزى", "ضُؤْزى" and "ضَأْزى", on the pattern "فَعْلى" with fatḥa. But in the Qurʾān only "ضِيزى" is permissible, with an unhamzated yāʾ. The grammarians did not say that it is in its original form only because they do not know "فِعْلى" as an adjective pattern in the language; they know adjectives only on "فَعْلى" with fatḥa, like "سَكْرى" (drunk) and "غَضْبى" (angry), or with ḍamma, like "حُبْلى" (pregnant) and "فُضْلى" (most excellent). Likewise they said "مِشْيَةٌ حِيكى", which is a gait in which the walker struts; one says "ḥāka, yaḥīku" when he struts. So "حِيكى" too is for them "فَعْلى" «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; by the argument just given, the intended pattern is presumably فُعْلى, with ḍamma.]».

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿وَما يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الهَوى﴾, that is: nothing that he brings you is something he has said from his own desire.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿إنْ هو إلا وحْيٌ يُوحى﴾: "إنْ" is in the sense of "ما" (negation); the meaning is: "It is nothing but revelation."

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ القُوى﴾: by this He means Jibrīl, peace be upon him.

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿ذُو مِرَّةٍ فاسْتَوى﴾: "ذُو مِرَّةٍ" is a naʿt (adjective) of His saying ﴿شَدِيدُ القُوى﴾ [al-Najm: 5], and "اَلْمِرَّةُ" is strength. ﴿عَلَّمَهُ﴾ [al-Najm: 5]: he taught the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿فاسْتَوى﴾ [al-Najm: 6] ﴿وَهُوَ بِالأُفُقِ الأعْلى﴾: one of the philologists said that "هُوَ" here refers to the Prophet, peace be upon him, the meaning being: "So Jibrīl and the Prophet ﷺ rose up together on the highest horizon." But according to the philologists the like of this is not permissible except in poetry, unless it is like your saying "istawaytu anā wa-Zaydun" (I and Zayd became level); they consider "istawaytu wa-Zaydun" ugly. Rather the meaning is: "Jibrīl rose up while he was on the highest horizon, in his true form", because he used to appear to the Prophet ﷺ in the form of a man when he descended to him with revelation, and the Messenger of Allah wished to see him in his true form, so he rose up on the eastern horizon and filled the horizon. So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: Jibrīl rose up on the highest horizon in his own form.

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ دَنا فَتَدَلّى﴾: the meaning of "دَنا" and "تَدَلّى" is one, because the meaning is that he came near, and "تَدَلّى" means he increased in nearness. It is as you say: "qad danā fulānun minnī wa-qaruba" (So-and-so drew close to me and came near); and if you said "qad qaruba minnī wa-danā", it would be permissible.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿فَكانَ قابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أوْ أدْنى﴾: the meaning is: "The distance between him and the Messenger of Allah was the measure of two Arab bows, or nearer." This passage needs explanation, because someone may say: "أوْ" is either for doubt or not for doubt. If it is for doubt, it is impossible for this to be a place of doubt; and if its meaning is "rather nearer", i.e. rather closer, then what need was there to say ﴿فَكانَ قابَ قَوْسَيْنِ﴾? It should have been "he was nearer than two bows' length". The answer to this — and Allah knows best — is that the servants were addressed according to their language and the measure of their understanding, and they were told here what is said to one who estimates. So the meaning is: "He was, by your own estimate, the measure of two bows, or nearer than that", just as you say of something you estimate: "This is the measure of two spears, or less than two spears, or more." Something like this has already passed in His saying: ﴿وَأرْسَلْناهُ إلى مِائَةِ ألْفٍ أوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 147].

zajjaj:26-26.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَمْ مِن مَلَكٍ في السَّماواتِ لا تُغْنِي شَفاعَتُهم شَيْئًا﴾: it came as "شَفاعَتُهُمْ" (their intercession) although the wording is the wording of a singular; had it been said "شَفاعَتُهُ" (his intercession) it would have been permissible, but the meaning is the meaning of a group, because "كَمْ" is a question about a number and a statement of a large number — for "رُبَّ" is for paucity and "كَمْ" for abundance. The meaning of "شَفاعَتُهُمْ" here is explained by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ العَرْشَ ومَن حَوْلَهُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ ويُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ ويَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنا وسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَةً وعِلْمًا فاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تابُوا واتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 7], up to His saying: ﴿وَذَلِكَ هو الفَوْزُ العَظِيمُ﴾ [Ghāfir: 9]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they intercede only for those with whom He is pleased, and this is the interpretation of His saying: ﴿لا تُغْنِي شَفاعَتُهم شَيْئًا إلا مِن بَعْدِ أنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَن يَشاءُ ويَرْضى﴾.

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالآخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ المَلائِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ الأُنْثى﴾ ﴿وَما لَهم بِهِ مِن عِلْمٍ﴾ [al-Najm: 28], that is: they say that the angels are the daughters of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:30-30.t: And His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهم مِنَ العِلْمِ﴾: because He described them as wanting nothing but the life of this world, and said: ﴿فَأعْرِضْ عَنْ مَن تَوَلّى عَنْ ذِكْرِنا ولَمْ يُرِدْ إلا الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا﴾ [al-Najm: 29] ﴿ذَلِكَ مَبْلَغُهم مِنَ العِلْمِ﴾: they know only what they need for their livelihood, for they have cast the matter of the Hereafter behind their backs.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبائِرَ الإثْمِ والفَواحِشَ إلا اللَّمَمَ﴾: it has been said that al-lamam is such things as a kiss, a glance and what resembles that. And it has been said: "إلّا اللَّمَمَ" means: except that the servant has touched upon (alamma bi-) an indecency and then repented.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ واسِعُ المَغْفِرَةِ﴾ indicates that al-lamam is that a person has touched upon a sin without persisting in it or remaining in it. In the language, ilmām (touching upon) entails that you come to a thing at a given time and do not stay at it. This — and Allah knows best — is the meaning of al-lamam in this place.

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَرَأيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلّى﴾ ﴿وَأعْطى قَلِيلا وأكْدى﴾ [al-Najm: 34]: the meaning of "أكْدى" is: he stopped. Its origin is from digging a well: it is said of the digger, when he digs the well and reaches a rock with which digging is impossible for him, "qad balagha ilā l-kudya" (he has reached the hard rock), and at that point he stops digging.

zajjaj:35-35.t: And His saying: ﴿أعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الغَيْبِ فَهو يَرى﴾: its meaning is: so he knows. Seeing (ruʾya) is of two kinds: one of them is "raʾaytu" meaning "I saw with my eyes", and the other is "I knew", as when you say "raʾaytu Zaydan akhāka wa-ṣadīqaka" (I considered Zayd your brother and your friend), whose meaning is "I knew". Do you not see that a blind man says "raʾaytu Zaydan ʿāqilan" (I considered Zayd intelligent)? If it were from seeing with the eye, it would not be permissible.

zajjaj:36-36.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِما في صُحُفِ مُوسى﴾ ﴿وَإبْراهِيمَ الَّذِي وفّى﴾ [al-Najm: 37], that is: who fulfilled. It is said that Ibrāhīm ﷺ fulfilled what he was commanded and the trial with which he was tested — the sacrifice of his son — for he resolved upon it until Allah ransomed him with a sacrifice; and he was tested with patience in the face of his people's enmity when the fire was kindled for him and he was cast into it; and he was also commanded to be circumcised, and he was circumcised. And it has been said "وَفّى" (with a doubled fāʾ) and it is more intensive than "وَفى" (with a single fāʾ), because what he was tested with was among the greatest of trials. And the meaning of ﴿أمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِما في صُحُفِ مُوسى﴾ ﴿وَإبْراهِيمَ﴾ [al-Najm: 37] is: "Or has he not been informed?" Then He made known what is in the scriptures.

zajjaj:38-38.t: The position of ﴿ألا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى﴾ is genitive (khafḍ); the meaning is: "Or has he not been informed that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another?!" "أنْ" here is a badal (substitute) for "ما". It is also permissible for "أنْ" to be in the position of the nominative, with "هُوَ" implied, as though, when it was said ﴿بِما في صُحُفِ مُوسى﴾ [al-Najm: 36], it was asked: "What is it?", and it was said: "It is ﴿ألا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى﴾." Its meaning is: no soul is taken to account for the sin of another. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَأنْ لَيْسَ لِلإنْسانِ إلا ما سَعى﴾ [al-Najm: 39], that is: this too is among what is in the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā, peace be upon them both. Its meaning is: man has nothing but the recompense of his striving; if he does good he is recompensed with good, and if he does evil he is recompensed with evil. "تَزِرُ" is from "wazara, yaziru", when one earns a wizr, which is sin.

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرى﴾: if someone says: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sees the deed of every doer and knows it, so what is the meaning of ﴿سَوْفَ يُرى﴾? The meaning is that the servant will see his striving on the Day of Resurrection, that is: he will see his deeds in his balance.

zajjaj:41-41.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يُجْزاهُ الجَزاءَ الأوْفى﴾, that is: he will be recompensed for his deeds with the fullest recompense. It is permissible to read "سَوْفَ يَرى", but the better is "يُرى", because your saying "inna Zaydan sawfa ukrimu" (Zayd — I will honour) has weakness in it, since "أنَّ" is an operator (ʿāmil) and "أُكْرِمُ" is an operator, and the noun cannot be made accusative from two directions. But it is permissible with the hāʾ (pronoun) implied, in the sense of "سَوْفَ يَراهُ" (he will see it), or with the hāʾ implied in "أنَّ": you say "inna Zaydan saʾukrimu" in the sense of "Zaydun saʾukrimu" «[Translator's note: the printed text has زيدًا with "إنّ"; for the pronoun-in-"أنّ" analysis the intended form is presumably إنّه زيدٌ سأُكرِم, i.e. "Zayd is one I will honour" with the nominative.]».

zajjaj:42-42.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَأنَّ إلى رَبِّكَ المُنْتَهى﴾, that is: to Him is the return. All of this is in the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿وَأنَّهُ هو أغْنى وأقْنى﴾: two views have been stated about "أقْنى". One of them is that "أقْنى" means "he made content"; and the other is that "أقْنى" means he granted him a qinya (lasting possession), that is: he made wealth a firm, abiding asset for its owner. From this is your saying "qadi qtanaytu kadhā wa-kadhā" (I have acquired such-and-such), that is: I have acted so that it stays with me and I do not let it go out of my hand.

zajjaj:49-49.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأنَّهُ هو رَبُّ الشِّعْرى﴾: "اَلشِّعْرى" (Sirius) is a star behind Orion (al-jawzāʾ), and it is one of the two stars of the Lion's Forearm (dhirāʿ al-asad). A tribe of the Arabs used to worship al-Shiʿrā, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that He is its Lord and its Creator, and that He is the One worshipped, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿وَأنَّهُ أهْلَكَ عادًا الأُولى﴾: these are the people of Hūd, and they are the first ʿĀd. As for "الأُولى", there are three dialectal forms of it: with sukūn on the lām and the hamza retained, which is the best of the forms; the next in quality is "اَلُولى", with ḍamma on the lām and the hamza dropped. By analogy, once the lām is vowelled the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) ought to drop, because the connecting alif was brought in only because of the lām's sukūn; but its retention is permissible because the alif of the definite article's lām does not drop with the interrogative alif, so it differs from the other connecting alifs. And among the Arabs are those who say "لُولى", meaning "اَلْأُولى", dropping the hamza because the lām is vowelled. It has been read "عادًا اللُّولى" according to this dialect, with the nunation assimilated into the lām; but the majority reading is "عادًا الأُولى", with the nunation given kasra.

zajjaj:51-51.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَثَمُودَ فَما أبْقى﴾: "ثَمُودَ" is conjoined (nasaq) to "عادًا". It is not permissible for it to be made accusative by His saying ﴿فَما أبْقى﴾, because what comes after the fāʾ does not govern what precedes it: you do not say "Zaydan fa-ḍarabtu" — so how much less when "ما" comes after the fāʾ! Most grammarians do not make what precedes the fāʾ accusative by what follows it. The meaning is: "And He destroyed Thamūd and did not spare them."

zajjaj:53-53.t:
﴿والمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أهْوى﴾: "اَلْمُؤْتَفِكَةُ" is the one that was swallowed up by the earth, that is: it was overturned with its people. The meaning of "أهْوى" is: it was raised, when they were swallowed up, towards the sky, until those in the heaven heard the voices of the people of the city of Lūṭ's people; then it was made to fall (uhwiyat), that is: it was cast into the abyss.
﴿فَغَشّاها ما غَشّى﴾ [al-Najm: 54]: its meaning is: "So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, covered it with the punishment that covered it."

zajjaj:55-55.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَبِأيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمارى﴾: this — and Allah knows best — is an address to man. When He enumerated to him what Allah had done for him, of the things that indicate His oneness, the meaning was: "O man, which of the favours of your Lord, which show you that He is One, do you doubt?" — because doubt is in man «[Translator's note: so literally in the source (لأنّ المرءَ به الشكّ); the point is presumably that tamārā is from mirāʾ, doubt.]».

zajjaj:56-56.t: And His saying: ﴿هَذا نَذِيرٌ مِنَ النُّذُرِ الأُولى﴾, that is: the Prophet ﷺ follows, in warning, the course of the prophets who preceded him, Allah's blessings be upon them. And it may be in the sense of: "This is a warning to you, just as those before you were warned; and you have been informed, by what Allah has narrated to you, of the state of those who denied the messengers and the destruction that befell them."

zajjaj:57-57.t: And His saying: ﴿أزِفَتِ الآزِفَةُ﴾: its meaning is: the near one has drawn near. You say "qad azifa l-shayʾu" when a thing comes near and approaches. This is like ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ﴾ [al-Qamar: 1].

zajjaj:58-58.t: And the meaning of ﴿لَيْسَ لَها مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ كاشِفَةٌ﴾: its meaning is: no one uncovers the knowledge of when it will be except Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا يُجَلِّيها لِوَقْتِها إلا هُوَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 187].

zajjaj:59-59.t: ﴿أفَمِن هَذا الحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ﴾, that is: at what is recited to you of the Book of Allah ﴿تَعْجَبُونَ﴾ ﴿وَتَضْحَكُونَ ولا تَبْكُونَ﴾ [al-Najm: 60] ﴿وَأنْتُمْ سامِدُونَ﴾ [al-Najm: 61]: its explanation is: heedlessly amusing yourselves.

zajjaj:62-62.t: And His saying: ﴿فاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ واعْبُدُوا﴾: its meaning is: "Prostrate to Allah who created the heavens and the earths, and do not worship al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, Manāt the third, the other, and al-Shiʿrā", because mention of the objects of their worship has occurred in this surah.
